tn_stephen_king_library.blurb: A compact sport crag in the South Clear Creek section of the Obed and Clear Creek climbing zone, on the Cumberland Plateau east of Knoxville. Twenty-two routes, almost all bolted with a pair of trad lines, tucked beneath a wide horizontal overhang that makes the cliff easy to recognise. The walk from the neighbouring cave is short. Expect steep, powerful, pumpy climbing rather than slabs: a couple of 5.7s and a few 5.10s open things up, but most lines sit in the 5.11 to 5.13 range, so this is a better stop for strong sport climbers than for newcomers. The wider South Clear Creek zone is popular and gets hot in summer, so cooler months suit it best.

tn_lower_leda.blurb: A small sandstone cliff north of Chattanooga, one of several distinct sections of the Leda climbing zone near Soddy-Daisy. Twenty-one routes, mostly bolted sport lines with half a dozen trad climbs, and a few set up for top-roping. Difficulty spreads widely: a handful of easy 5.5 to 5.8 lines make it workable for newer leaders, a solid middle block of 5.9 and 5.10 routes forms the bulk, and a few hard 5.12 and 5.13 lines cap it off. Stone quality is good for the region, and a short trail from the road gets you to the base in around ten minutes, making it a handy quick-hit crag.

tn_warm_up_boulder.blurb: The largest single cluster in the Cumberland Boulders, a sandstone bouldering zone on the edge of the Cumberland Plateau near Soddy-Daisy, reached along the Cumberland Trail. About twenty-one problems are packed tightly together, which makes it easy to link sessions without much walking. The range is broad: a few VB and V0 problems, a good run through V1 to V4 where most of the volume sits, and a handful of harder lines up to V8. As the name hints, it works well as a first stop for loosening up before moving on to the area's bigger roofs, and suits mixed groups with varied abilities.
tn_warm_up_boulder.parking_note: Leave the car at the Mowbray Pike Trailhead, 809 County Highway 1126 in Soddy-Daisy. From Dayton Pike turn onto Mountain Road, which becomes Mowbray Pike; the lot is about 2.5 miles along on the right.
tn_warm_up_boulder.approach: From the lot, follow the obvious Cumberland Trail path behind it for roughly half a mile or less. The boulder cluster lies to the right of the trail.
